SECTOR APPLICATION

Financial Sector in the United Kingdom

21 / 31

Existing frameworks apply

The FCA identifies the Consumer Duty and senior-management accountability as relevant foundations for firms’ use of AI.

Existing powers apply

The regulator can use its supervisory and enforcement powers where a firm’s use of AI breaches relevant financial regulatory requirements.

Responsibilities follow the firm’s activities and its documented management arrangements. Avoid assigning all AI risk to the chief technology officer, or creating a new title without decision authority.

The FCA explains that its existing frameworks apply to firms' use of AI. Its approach identifies the Consumer Duty and senior-management accountability as relevant foundations. The regulator can use its existing supervisory and enforcement powers where a firm's use of AI breaches the relevant financial regulatory requirements.

Responsibilities should follow the firm's activities and its documented management arrangements. A business decision, a technology system and a risk control may involve different people, but their responsibilities must connect. Avoid assigning all AI risk automatically to the chief technology officer or creating a new title without decision authority.

For a credit-decisioning tool, the firm should establish who owns the lending use, who challenges the risk assessment and who authorises deployment. Supplier testing can contribute evidence. It does not remove the firm's responsibility for how the tool is used.
